title: Cryptographic Failures

levels.beginner: Cryptography fails most often not because the maths is broken, but because it is used wrongly: passwords stored in plain text, sensitive data sent without TLS, old algorithms kept running, or keys left in source code.
levels.intermediate: Watch for: data in transit without TLS, sensitive data at rest unencrypted, weak or outdated algorithms (MD5/SHA-1 for passwords, DES, RC4), hard-coded keys and secrets, and random numbers from a non-cryptographic generator used for tokens.
levels.advanced: Rules that cover most cases: TLS everywhere with modern configuration; encrypt sensitive data at rest with a managed key; hash passwords with Argon2id/bcrypt/scrypt; use a vetted library and a cryptographic random generator for tokens and keys; rotate keys and never commit them.

key_points: TLS for all traffic; no sensitive data over plain HTTP.
Hash passwords with a purpose-built password hash (Argon2id), never MD5/SHA-1.
Use a vetted crypto library; do not design your own cipher or protocol.
Keys and secrets live in a vault or environment, never in code or git.
Use a cryptographic random source for tokens, salts and keys.

defensive_examples.title: Cryptographically secure random token
defensive_examples.code:
import secrets
token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)  # random, URL-safe, suitable for session/reset tokens
defensive_examples.explanation: The secrets module uses the operating system's secure random source. The random module is for simulations, not security tokens.

defensive_examples.title: Password hashing, not encryption
defensive_examples.code:
# Passwords are HASHED (one-way) with Argon2id, not encrypted.
# Encryption is reversible with a key; a hash cannot be reversed,
# so a database leak does not hand attackers the passwords.
defensive_examples.explanation: Hashing is the right tool for passwords because the server never needs to recover the original password — it only needs to check a guess.

knowledge_check.question: Which is the correct way to store user passwords?
options: Store in plain text for recovery
Encrypt with a key in the same database
knowledge_check.explanation: A memory-hard password hash is one-way and slow to guess. Plain text, reversible encryption and fast hashes like MD5 all fail when the database leaks.

knowledge_check.question: Why should session tokens come from a cryptographic random source?
options: So they cannot be predicted or guessed by an attacker
knowledge_check.explanation: Predictable tokens let an attacker forge a session. A secure random source makes guessing infeasible.
